# ELE680 — SAC width comparison: 2×256 vs 2×512 (HalfCheetah-v5)

*Generated by `analysis/plot_width_comparison.py`; every number below is computed from the tracked run files.*
**Descriptive analysis of n = 3 training seeds per architecture. No claim of statistical significance is made.**

## 1. Data validation (all six runs passed)

Checked per run: completed status at 1,000,000 steps; HalfCheetah-v5; seed in config and metadata;
config.json identical to the config recorded in metadata.json; exact scientific Git commit and clean tree;
parameter count; hidden width (baseline configs omit `hidden_width`, interpreted as the frozen default 256);
exactly 40 periodic evaluations at 25k…1M (5 episodes each) and one final 10-episode evaluation at 1M;
metadata/CSV final return agreement; finite evaluation and training diagnostics.
Cross-run check: every config field except `seed`, `run_id` and `hidden_width` is identical across all six runs.

| architecture   |   seed | git_commit   | git_dirty   |   hidden_width |   total_params |   final_mean_return_10ep |   final_within_seed_episode_sd |   runtime_hours |
|:---------------|-------:|:-------------|:------------|---------------:|---------------:|-------------------------:|-------------------------------:|----------------:|
| 2×256          |      0 | 1a9f240      | False       |            256 |         217870 |                  12250.5 |                         133.93 |            5.29 |
| 2×256          |      1 | 1a9f240      | False       |            256 |         217870 |                  11335.9 |                          66.36 |            5.08 |
| 2×256          |      2 | 1a9f240      | False       |            256 |         217870 |                  12132.4 |                         117.24 |           12.33 |
| 2×512          |      0 | f25b3a0      | False       |            512 |         828942 |                  11552.7 |                         175.84 |            5.05 |
| 2×512          |      1 | f25b3a0      | False       |            512 |         828942 |                  12167.2 |                          51.57 |            4.82 |
| 2×512          |      2 | f25b3a0      | False       |            512 |         828942 |                  11216.2 |                          91.15 |            5.04 |

Baseline commit `1a9f2405b5fdb9cffa379b72f569a0a3a01515e4`, width commit `f25b3a0cb93da0a605b3dbac6254a866f83f664e`.
The commits differ because `f25b3a0` added the configurable-width code. The default-width (256) path is covered by
unit tests, but the baseline runs were not re-executed on the newer commit.

## 2. Final performance (separate 10-episode final evaluation)

| Architecture | Final return, mean ± sample SD across 3 seeds | Per-seed values |
|---|---|---|
| 2×256 | 11,906.25 ± 497.45 | 12,250.5, 11,335.9, 12,132.4 |
| 2×512 | 11,645.37 ± 482.26 | 11,552.7, 12,167.2, 11,216.2 |

- Difference (2×512 − 2×256): **-260.9** (-2.19%); pooled SD 489.9;
  Cohen's d = -0.53, Hedges' g = -0.43 (small-sample corrected); Welch SE of the difference 400.0.
- The difference is about half of the between-seed SD and the seed ranges overlap
  (2×256: 11,336–12,250; 2×512: 11,216–12,167).
- Exploratory exact permutation test: two-sided p = 0.60. With 3 vs 3 seeds the smallest attainable
  p is 0.10, so this test cannot reach conventional significance whatever the data.
- The between-seed SD is **not** the within-seed episode SD (final-evaluation episode SD per run:
  52–176), and neither is a confidence interval.
- The periodic 1M-step evaluation (5 episodes) shares deterministic episode seeds with the final evaluation, is not independent,
  and is not used for the headline comparison.

## 3. Learning curves, sample efficiency and checkpoints

Mean periodic return (5 episodes) per checkpoint, mean ± between-seed sample SD:

|    step | architecture   |   eval_return_mean |   eval_return_sd_between_seeds |
|--------:|:---------------|-------------------:|-------------------------------:|
|   25000 | 2×256          |             2052.7 |                          365.7 |
|   25000 | 2×512          |             1735.7 |                          459   |
|  100000 | 2×256          |             6472.7 |                          173.9 |
|  100000 | 2×512          |             5967.3 |                          306.6 |
|  250000 | 2×256          |             9428.8 |                          321.2 |
|  250000 | 2×512          |             8765.4 |                          852.1 |
|  500000 | 2×256          |            10553   |                          107.7 |
|  500000 | 2×512          |            10294.5 |                          651.3 |
|  750000 | 2×256          |            11325.1 |                          161.4 |
|  750000 | 2×512          |            10388.8 |                         1916.3 |
| 1000000 | 2×256          |            11881.2 |                          520   |
| 1000000 | 2×512          |            11663.5 |                          475.8 |

- Mean of the 40 periodic evaluations (area-under-curve proxy), 2×256 vs 2×512: 9,911.5 ± 146.1 vs
  9,560.3 ± 634.2; difference -351.2 (-3.5%), Hedges' g = -0.61.
- First evaluation step at which a seed's mean return reaches a threshold (seeds 0, 1, 2):

| Threshold | 2×256 | 2×512 |
|---|---|---|
| 5000 | 75k, 75k, 75k | 75k, 75k, 100k |
| 8000 | 175k, 150k, 175k | 200k, 175k, 225k |
| 10000 | 375k, 350k, 350k | 525k, 325k, 475k |

- In this sample the 2×512 mean curve is below the 2×256 mean curve at every checkpoint tabulated, and the seed-wise threshold
  steps are equal or later for 2×512 in most cases. The mean gaps at the tabulated checkpoints (218–936 return units) are of the same order as the
  between-seed SDs, although they exceed the baseline's own SD at several checkpoints; the 2×512 SD at 750k is inflated by
  low-return outlier episodes in seed 2 (see section 4 and figure 07). The 2×512 mean is below the 2×256 mean at 36 of 40 evaluation points. The mean gap averages -643 over steps ≤ 300k
  and -226 over steps > 300k, i.e. it is largest early and narrows later (figure 07), but this pattern rests on 3 seeds per arm.
  **The data do not support a claim that width 512 improves sample efficiency, and are insufficient to claim it hurts it.**

## 4. Stability

| Metric (mean ± SD across seeds) | 2×256 | 2×512 |
|---|---|---|
| SD of periodic returns, steps ≥ 750k | 321 ± 65 | 512 ± 342 |
| Largest drop below running-best periodic return | 578 ± 121 | 1,128 ± 1,083 |
| Periodic evals after 500k containing a low-return outlier episode¹ (seeds 0, 1, 2) | [0, 0, 0] | [0, 0, 2] |

¹ Low-return outlier episode: an evaluation episode whose return is below 0.5 × the median episode return of the
same 5-episode evaluation. This is a descriptive heuristic only; it does not identify why an episode scored low.

- The higher 2×512 averages are driven by one run. 2×512 seed 2 has two isolated evaluation dips (750k and 800k) whose
  within-evaluation SD is about 2,900. At 750k one of the five deterministic episodes returned about 3,000 and two others about 8,000–9,000;
  at 800k one returned about 3,700. The policy is back near 10,800 at the following evaluations (775k, 825k). Seeds 0 and 1 of 2×512 resemble the baseline seeds on these measures. One seed is not evidence of a general
  width-related instability, nor of its absence.
- No run shows a persistent collapse, and all logged diagnostics are finite.

- Critic loss, |Q| and critic gradient norm are lower for 2×512 at 100k–500k in this sample, and alpha is slightly lower;
  by 750k–1M the two are close for loss, |Q| and alpha. Three seeds cannot show whether the earlier differences are meaningful.
- Losses and gradient norms are large in absolute terms for both architectures; scale alone is not evidence of pathology.

### Critic-loss spikes (descriptive, not a divergence test)

A spike event is a contiguous run of logged points above 10× the centred 25-point rolling median.

| architecture   |   seed |   critic_loss_spikes_10x_median | critic_loss_spike_steps            |   critic_loss_max |
|:---------------|-------:|--------------------------------:|:-----------------------------------|------------------:|
| 2×256          |      0 |                               1 | 506001                             |             486.3 |
| 2×256          |      1 |                               3 | 504001;894001;912001               |            1274.8 |
| 2×256          |      2 |                               0 |                                    |             147.4 |
| 2×512          |      0 |                               0 |                                    |             131   |
| 2×512          |      1 |                               0 |                                    |             225.7 |
| 2×512          |      2 |                               5 | 540001;591001;666001;821001;840001 |            2530.8 |

- Spike events occur in both architectures (2×256 seeds 0 and 1; 2×512 seed 2) and learning continues afterwards.
  The 2×512 seed-2 spikes (540k, 591k, 666k, 821k, 840k) do not coincide with its two evaluation dips (750k, 800k),
  so these data support no causal link. Spike counts per seed (1.3 ± 1.5 vs 1.7 ± 2.9) are uneven and rest on a handful of events.

## 6. Compute (observed, not controlled)

| Metric (seeds 0, 1, 2) | 2×256 | 2×512 |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime (h) | 5.29, 5.08, 12.33 | 5.05, 4.82, 5.04 |
| Final cumulative SPS | 52.5, 54.7, 22.5 | 55.1, 57.6, 55.2 |
| Median runtime excluding flagged runs (h) | 5.19 | 5.04 |

- Runs flagged as more than 1.5× the six-run median runtime: 2×256 seed 2. Its slowdown begins early in training (figure 03), is unexplained, and shared-GPU
  load was not recorded, so **throughput differences must not be attributed to architecture**. Excluding the flagged run, the
  runtimes of both architectures are similar (about 5 h) despite 3.8× more parameters (828,942 vs 217,870), suggesting the
  training loop is not dominated by network size on this hardware. This is an observation, not a controlled measurement.
- The all-seed baseline runtime mean in `width_comparison_stats.json` is distorted by the flagged run.

## 7. Conclusions and limitations

1. On HalfCheetah-v5 with this SAC configuration, 2×512 showed no final-return, sample-efficiency or stability advantage over 2×256.
   The point estimate is 2.2% lower final return, well within seed-to-seed variation.
2. This is compatible with H1 (naive width scaling does not guarantee better performance), but three seeds cannot establish it.
3. Limitations: n = 3 per architecture; one environment; one hyperparameter setting (not retuned for width);
   noisy 5-episode periodic evaluations; baseline and width runs come from different code commits; runtime confounded by
   shared-GPU load; one 2×512 seed (seed 2) accounts for most of the larger late-training variability observed in the 2×512 group.
4. Do not generalise from this single pair. The planned 2×1024 and depth studies are needed to see whether any trend is monotone.
